artist_statement.text:
**Morning Glory**

This photograph portrays the spillway funnel of the San Roque Dam in Córdoba, Argentina: a hydraulic engineering system designed to automatically regulate excess pressure from the reservoir. When the lake rises above a certain level, the water begins to overflow without the need for gates or human intervention, preventing floods in downstream communities.

The mechanism was built in 1944 as part of an expansion of the original dam, which depended on the manual opening of floodgates to release accumulated water pressure. More than eighty years later, it continues to operate under the same principle, managing excess, preserving reserves for dry seasons, and sustaining life in the region while minimizing operational risk. 

An infrastructure that, long before the internet, was already physically solving problems we now associate with permissionless design.


*Captured on May 12, 2026 at San Roque Dam, Córdoba, Argentina using a Xiaomi smartphone camera (f/2.2, ISO 100, 1/6s). Edited from RAW in Lightroom with minimal tonal adjustments and compositional cropping. Dimensions: 2670 × 1878 px.*

*This work will be released under CC0 if selected for acquisition by the 6529 Network Museum.*
